paragraphs.text: Dan and Maria lean out the treehouse window. "This one will go farther, I know it!" shouts Dan. He tosses a paper airplane. Flop! It falls straight to the ground.

"One more," says Dan. He tries to fold another plane, but something looks wrong. This one has a different shape. It has four wings instead of two! "This probably won't fly," Dan says with a sigh. But he tries anyway. It spins in circles through the air and floats slowly to the ground.
"Wow! It looks like a butterfly!" Maria cheers. Dan grins. He wanted a paper airplane, but this is even better.
Maria gives Dan a high five. "Show me how to make one!" she says.
Dan shows Maria how to fold the paper to make four wings. Soon, little paper butterflies fill the yard.

content.text: What is the story mostly about?

contents.text: When you read, it is important to make sure you understand what the story is trying to tell you.
First, think about the topic. The topic is what the story is about. For example, the topic might be "playing with friends."

Next, think about the theme. The theme is the lesson or message of the story. It is what the author wants the reader to learn about the topic. For example, if the topic of a story is "playing with friends," the theme might be "It is good to share."

A story does not always say the theme directly. You can guess it by thinking about what the characters say and do. Think about what the characters learn. Think about what you can learn from the characters.

paragraphs.text: Dan and Maria lean out the treehouse window. "This one will go farther, I know it!" shouts Dan. He tosses a paper airplane. Flop! It falls straight to the ground.

"One more," says Dan. He tries to fold another plane, but something looks wrong. This one has a different shape. It has four wings instead of two! "This probably won't fly," Dan says with a sigh. But he tries anyway. It spins in circles through the air and floats slowly to the ground.
"Wow! It looks like a butterfly!" Maria cheers. Dan grins. He wanted a paper airplane, but this is even better.
Maria gives Dan a high five. "Show me how to make one!" she says.
Dan shows Maria how to fold the paper to make four wings. Soon, little paper butterflies fill the yard.

contents.text: When you read, it is important to make sure you understand what the story is trying to tell you.
First, think about the topic. The topic is what the story is about. For example, the topic might be "playing with friends."

Next, think about the theme. The theme is the lesson or message of the story. It is what the author wants the reader to learn about the topic. For example, if the topic of a story is "playing with friends," the theme might be "It is good to share."

A story does not always say the theme directly. You can guess it by thinking about what the characters say and do. Think about what the characters learn. Think about what you can learn from the characters.
